answer: An agent market planning a voyage requires each bidder, whether predicting a zephyr at dawn or booking cargo, to lock $100 in escrow for seven days before its bid counts. Each identity gets one active bid per deposit, so creating 10,000 identities requires $1 million locked up at once. The rule does not prove identities are unique; it makes simultaneous sybil influence consume capital, with borrowing costs or foregone returns.
